content: The continuing medical education (CME) program is a collaborative effort between the Duke University Health System Department of Clinical Education and Professional Development and The WikiDoc Foundation. This program is designed as an Internet Point-of-Care CME activity, allowing physicians to engage in self-directed online learning tailored to their clinical practice. Participants are required to document their clinical questions, the resources they consulted, and how the information is applied to their practice. This reflective process is integral to the learning activity. The program was first made available on November 1, 2015, and expired on November 1, 2016. Each search conducted as part of this activity is estimated to take approximately 30 minutes. For every cumulative 30 minutes of activity on the WikiDoc platform, participants can claim 0.5 CME credits (AMA PRA Category 1 Credit™). There is no limit to the number of Internet Point-of-Care cycles that physicians can complete using WikiDoc. Evidence suggests that only about 25% of physicians implement evidence-based guidelines within seven years of their endorsement by international societies. Furthermore, it can take up to seven years for 50% of physicians in relevant specialties to adopt nationally endorsed evidence-based guidelines. WikiDoc addresses this gap by providing healthcare professionals with regularly updated medical information, including the latest evidence-based guidelines and nationally endorsed recommendations. This platform aims to democratize access to medical knowledge, breaking down traditional silos and fostering collaboration among healthcare providers. WikiDoc was created to promote the free exchange of medical knowledge and to encourage collaboration among healthcare professionals. The increasing specialization within medicine has led to fragmented care, with limited sharing of expertise across specialties. By using the WikiDoc platform, healthcare professionals can collaborate with peers, share valuable knowledge, and enhance both clinical practice and medical education. The content provided through WikiDoc CME activities is designed to benefit a wide range of users, including: Attending physicians and independent practitioners: To enhance their general medical knowledge, prepare for subspecialty board exams, and assist in teaching medical students and residents. Housestaff: To prepare for morning reports and as a quick reference during hospital rounds. Medical students: To prepare for morning rounds, research patient conditions, and study for USMLE exams using board review materials. Fellows: To prepare for conferences, teach on hospital wards, and study for specialty board exams. Nursing and ancillary staff: To access information on patient management, medications, and dosing. Patients: To learn more about their own medical conditions or those of their family members through WikiPatient pages. This activity has been planned and implemented by the Duke University Health System Department of Clinical Education and Professional Development and The WikiDoc Foundation to advance patient care. The Duke University Health System Department of Clinical Education and Professional Development is accredited by the American Nurses Credentialing Center (ANCC), the Accreditation Council for Pharmacy Education (ACPE), and the Accreditation Council for Continuing Medical Education (ACCME) to provide continuing education for healthcare teams. The department designates this Internet Point-of-Care activity for a maximum of 0.5 AMA PRA Category 1 Credits™. Physicians should only claim credit proportional to their participation in the activity. By registering for CME credit, participants' activities on WikiDoc, including browsing and editing, will be tracked. Participants can monitor their progress through the CME Tracker page, which logs activities based on the topics browsed. Users can select one or more activities for which they wish to claim CME credit. After verifying their log, participants will be prompted to complete a brief survey about the activity. Upon completing the survey, they can print a personalized CME certificate. The WikiDoc platform is compatible with Windows (XP, Vista, 7, 8, 8.1), Macintosh (OSX Yosemite, Mavericks, Mountain Lion, Snow Leopard, and Leopard), and Chrome OS. It supports all major web browsers, including Internet Explorer (v7 or higher), Safari (v6.0 or higher), Firefox (v10 or higher), and all versions of Google Chrome. Some content may require additional software, such as Macromedia Flash, Apple QuickTime, Adobe Acrobat, or Microsoft Office, to view multimedia, presentations, or printable materials.
